newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL noon rubber higher on Tokyo's gains, trade slow.
newsitem.headline: KL noon rubber higher on Tokyo's gains, trade slow.

text.p: Rubber prices in Malaysia were quoted higher at noon due to gains in Tokyo but trading was inactive, dealers said.
"There was little interest this morning. Prices moved up because of Tokyo," a dealer said. But he added that business was slow as buyers were mostly sidelined.
Currency uncertainty continued to caution the market.
Far East consumers continue to monitor prices closely but they have not shown a keen interest to buy. "We have sufficient stocks to supply if the prices are attractive to them," a trader said.
Dealers offered SMR CV at 294 cents, SMR L at 275, SMR 5 at 254, SMR 10 at 248, SMR 20 at 246 and latex at 190.
At noon, August RSS1 buyer rose half a cent to 249.50 cents (95 U.S. cents) and August SMR 20 buyer up two cents to 250.
Malaysia-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
